evidence.note: Agent lists the subtle numerical traps (clustering bootstrap, summarization per-prediction skip, classification shuffle composition) as things to 'be careful' about, but treats them as one-shot implementation concerns; never sets up any numerical cross-check or revisits them when results are produced.

The one genuine correctness fix (retrieval qrels 'relevance'→'score') is a crash/data-shape fix that produced a KeyError, not a response to an out-of-tolerance score. It is diagnosed by inspecting the qrels files, not by noticing a divergence from the leaderboard.
Hundreds of steps consumed by OOM and a stuck heredoc terminal. All debugging effort targets getting the code to run/finish, never whether the numbers match the reference.

Final 'verification' is explicitly structural only (metric keys present, numeric, no NaN/Inf) and the agent marks the task complete on that basis, having never compared any main_score to the mteb leaderboard or spec — i.e. it ships whatever the code produced.

reasoning: The dimension concerns revising the implementation when computed scores diverge from the leaderboard/spec and tracing the mismatch to the responsible protocol detail. Across the entire horizon the agent performed zero numerical cross-checking against the reference; its only correctness-adjacent fix (retrieval key) resolved a crash, not a score mismatch, and it ultimately validated and shipped purely on structural grounds. This matches the anchor-0/1 description ('ships whatever the code produces') rather than anchor 3+ (which requires at least reacting to an actual score mismatch). I set it at 1 to give slight credit for one genuine functional bug fix, but the numerical-divergence debugging behavior this dimension measures is essentially absent.
